subject: zoology
question_text: What is meant by tautonymy? Give two examples.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.49, VSAQ 63). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. ADDED BEYOND THE BOOK: the line that tautonymy is allowed in animal naming but not in plant naming is standard and is not printed in this book's answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What tautonymy is
steps.why: The definition is about the two words matching, so the test for tautonymy is to read the scientific name and see the same word twice.
common_mistakes: Confusing it with trinomial naming. Tautonymy has two words that are the same, not three words.
Giving a plant example. Tautonymy is not allowed under the plant code, so every example is an animal.
steps.memory_tip: Tauto means same: the same word twice, genus then species.
steps.margin_note: One sentence, then the two examples. Do not write more.
lines: Tautonymy is the practice of naming an animal
in which the generic name and the specific
It is allowed in animal naming under the ICZN.

steps.label: The two examples
steps.why: Two examples are asked, so each name is written with the animal it belongs to — the name alone does not show what it is.
common_mistakes: Giving only one example. The question asks for two.
steps.memory_tip: Naja naja and Axis axis: read each name aloud and the word repeats.
steps.margin_note: Two names with the animal each one belongs to. Two lines.
lines: Naja naja is the Indian cobra.
Axis axis is the spotted deer.

insider_note: Tautonymy is valid in zoology but not in botany, so a plant example scores nothing — keep to animals such as Naja naja and Axis axis.
